verses.text: "Why doesn't the Almighty set times for judgment? Why don't those who know him get to see those days?
People move boundary stones and steal flocks, then graze the animals as their own.
They drive off the orphans' donkey and take the widow's ox as security for a debt.
They push the needy off the road, and the poor of the land all go into hiding.
Like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go out to work, searching hard for food. The wilderness provides bread for their children.
They cut what they can eat in the fields and gather leftovers in the vineyards of the wicked.
They spend the night naked, with no clothes and nothing to cover themselves in the cold.
They're soaked by mountain showers and cling to the rocks because they have no shelter.
Some people tear a fatherless child from the breast and take what little the poor have as security for a debt.
The poor go around naked, without clothing, and they carry bundles of grain while going hungry.
They press oil between their oppressors' walls and tread their winepresses while going thirsty.
People groan in the crowded city, and the wounded cry for help, yet God pays no attention to the wrongdoing.
There are people who rebel against the light. They don't know its ways or stay on its paths.
The murderer gets up at daylight and kills the poor and needy. At night he acts like a thief.
The adulterer watches for dusk, thinking, 'No one will see me,' and covers his face.
In the dark they break into houses, and by day they shut themselves inside. They want nothing to do with the light.
Morning is like deep darkness to them, because they're at home with the terrors of the dark.
They're like foam on the surface of the water. Their share of the land is cursed, and they no longer go down the path to the vineyards.
As drought and heat swallow up the melted snow, Sheol swallows up those who've sinned.
Even the womb that bore them forgets them. Worms feast on them, and no one remembers them anymore. Wrongdoing is snapped like a tree.
They prey on women who have no children and show no kindness to widows.
Yet God keeps the powerful alive by his strength. They get up again when they have no assurance of life.
God gives them security, and they rest in it, while his eyes watch what they do.
They're lifted high for a little while, then they're gone. They're brought low and taken away like everyone else, cut off like the heads of grain.
If that isn't true, who can prove I'm lying and show that my words are worthless?"
